name: history and corpus
owns: thirty years of public record: advisories, disclosures, conference talks, writeups, patches, and the patterns buried in them
why_in_D: This is the only lens that holds evidence about what has already happened. Every other lens can be reasoned about; this one cannot, because the answer is a fact about the past. It is also the only lens where the corpus is bigger than anyone can read, which makes the method of mining it part of the subject.

factors.name: advisory corpus coverage
factors.def: which databases the corpus draws from and the overlap between them
factors.observable: a CVE present in one database and absent from another

factors.name: CVE to code mapping
factors.def: whether an advisory can be tied to a specific commit or function
factors.observable: a fix commit identified from an advisory

factors.name: advisory richness
factors.def: whether the record states cause and mechanism or only product and version
factors.observable: an advisory with no technical detail

factors.name: silent patch rate
factors.def: the fraction of fixes shipped with no advisory at all
factors.observable: a security fixed commit with no associated identifier

factors.name: retroactive assignment lag
factors.def: the delay between a fix and the advisory that names it
factors.observable: a fixed issue with an advisory issued years later

factors.name: CWE label reliability
factors.def: whether the assigned weakness class reflects the actual mechanism
factors.observable: a mislabelled advisory reclassified on reading

factors.name: CVSS score bias
factors.def: whether the score reflects demonstrable impact or an author's estimate
factors.observable: a score contradicted by observed exploitability

factors.name: exploit availability timing
factors.def: how quickly public exploit code appears after disclosure
factors.observable: time from advisory to a working public exploit

factors.name: in the wild exploitation confirmation
factors.def: whether exploitation has been independently observed
factors.observable: evidence beyond the reporter's claim

factors.name: disclosure channel bias
factors.def: which classes of issue are reported publicly and which are quietly fixed
factors.observable: a class underrepresented in public data

factors.name: research duplication
factors.def: how often the same mechanism is independently described by several authors
factors.observable: two writeups describing one mechanism under different names

factors.name: naming inconsistency
factors.def: whether the same technique carries several names, which fragments the record
factors.observable: one technique found by several search terms

factors.name: conference archive completeness
factors.def: which talk archives are indexed and which are only video
factors.observable: a technique documented only in a recording

factors.name: sliding history
factors.def: how quickly technique knowledge becomes obsolete as frameworks change
factors.observable: a documented technique that no longer applies to current versions

factors.name: resurrection rate
factors.def: how often an old technique returns in a new context
factors.observable: a technique from a decade ago working again

factors.name: framework version to technique mapping
factors.def: whether a technique is tied to a version range or to a general shape
factors.observable: a technique stated for one version only

factors.name: patch revert frequency
factors.def: how often a security fix is reverted for breaking behaviour
factors.observable: a fix reverted and the issue returning

factors.name: incomplete fix rate
factors.def: how often a fix covers one instance of a class and not the class
factors.observable: a bypass of a published fix

factors.name: regression across versions
factors.def: whether a fixed issue reappears in a later rewrite
factors.observable: the same mechanism working in a newer version

factors.name: bug bounty disclosure detail
factors.def: how much of a public report survives redaction
factors.observable: a report where the mechanism is visible

factors.name: writeup quality distribution
factors.def: the fraction of public writeups that state a reproducible procedure
factors.observable: a writeup with no steps

factors.name: copy propagation in writeups
factors.def: how many writeups restate an earlier one without adding evidence
factors.observable: identical phrasing across independent sources

factors.name: unverifiable claim prevalence
factors.def: how many public claims cannot be checked by anyone
factors.observable: a claim with no artefact

factors.name: vendor advisory hedging
factors.def: whether a vendor describes impact minimisingly
factors.observable: an advisory whose wording understates the demonstrated effect

factors.name: coordinated disclosure timeline adherence
factors.def: whether the 90 day norm was met or the deadline was extended under pressure
factors.observable: days from report to publication

factors.name: suppression pressure
factors.def: whether reports were delayed or buried for commercial reasons
factors.observable: a disclosure pattern inconsistent with the norm

factors.name: zero day lifetime estimate
factors.def: the observed time between use in the wild and public knowledge
factors.observable: a campaign later matched to an advisory

factors.name: exploit kit lifecycle
factors.def: how fast a technique moves from research to commodity tooling
factors.observable: a research technique appearing in a scanner

factors.name: scanner signature lag
factors.def: how long after disclosure a mainstream scanner detects the issue
factors.observable: a vulnerable target missed by a scanner

factors.name: taxonomy drift
factors.def: how the same issue is classified across frameworks, and where they disagree
factors.observable: one issue mapped to different classes by two frameworks

factors.name: framework coverage gaps
factors.def: which frameworks no public corpus covers well
factors.observable: a framework with no structured test list

factors.name: language and region bias
factors.def: which languages and regions are over or under represented in the public record
factors.observable: a technique documented only in a non English source

factors.name: archive loss
factors.def: how much of the record has already rotted
factors.observable: a dead link where the primary source was

factors.name: link rot rate in security documentation
factors.def: the fraction of cited URLs that no longer resolve
factors.observable: measured failure rate over a sample

factors.name: primary source availability
factors.def: whether the original report exists or only a secondary summary
factors.observable: a claim traceable only to a blog citing a blog

factors.name: artifact preservation practice
factors.def: whether proof of concept code is archived, since repositories get deleted
factors.observable: a PoC repository that no longer exists

factors.name: code archaeology feasibility
factors.def: whether the vulnerable code can still be obtained at the right version
factors.observable: an old version retrieved and built

factors.name: dependency history reconstruction
factors.def: whether the dependency tree of an old build can be recovered
factors.observable: a lockfile from the affected era

factors.name: patch diff reading
factors.def: whether the fix's diff reveals the mechanism better than the advisory
factors.observable: a mechanism understood from the diff alone

factors.name: commit message informativeness
factors.def: whether the message states security relevance
factors.observable: a commit silently fixing a serious issue

factors.name: metering the corpus
factors.def: how many distinct techniques the public record actually contains after deduplication
factors.observable: a deduplicated count with a stated method

factors.name: coverage of the corpus by any single list
factors.def: the largest fraction of the corpus one collection holds
factors.observable: a union analysis across collections

factors.name: long tail shape
factors.def: how much of the corpus appears in exactly one source
factors.observable: the fraction unique to one collection

factors.name: entry quality in harvested lists
factors.def: how many harvested rows are tools, headings, badges or dead projects
factors.observable: a disposition count by row kind

factors.name: duplicate rate across collections
factors.def: how much the collections overlap
factors.observable: the intersection size

factors.name: stale collection detection
factors.def: whether a list is maintained, which decides whether its absence means absence
factors.observable: last push date against the current date

factors.name: archived collection handling
factors.def: whether an archived list is treated as a snapshot rather than a live source
factors.observable: an archived repo cited as current

factors.name: star count as a proxy for quality
factors.def: whether popularity is mistaken for completeness
factors.observable: a highly starred list missing major areas

factors.name: entry liveness
factors.def: the fraction of listed tools that still exist and resolve
factors.observable: measured dead rate in a sample

factors.name: tool abandonment rate
factors.def: the fraction of listed tools with no release in a long window
factors.observable: last release date distribution

factors.name: historical severity distribution
factors.def: which mechanism classes produced the most serious real world incidents
factors.observable: an incident corpus classified by mechanism

factors.name: incident to technique mapping
factors.def: whether a real breach can be traced to a documented technique
factors.observable: an incident report matched to a pattern

factors.name: reported cause versus actual cause
factors.def: whether the public explanation of an incident matches the technical evidence
factors.observable: a cause contradicted by later analysis

factors.name: attribution noise
factors.def: how uncertain actor attribution is, and whether it changes the defensive lesson
factors.observable: conflicting attributions for one campaign

factors.name: benchmark and lab reuse
factors.def: whether a lab exists for a technique or only prose
factors.observable: a technique with a runnable environment

factors.name: test list provenance
factors.def: whether a framework item was written from practice or from theory
factors.observable: an item with no citation to a real finding

factors.name: community correction speed
factors.def: how quickly an error in a popular resource is corrected
factors.observable: a known error persisting across mirrors

factors.name: mirror divergence
factors.def: whether forks and mirrors of a resource differ from the original
factors.observable: a mirror missing later corrections

factors.name: translation fidelity
factors.def: whether a translated technique description preserves the mechanism
factors.observable: a translated page whose technical claims differ

factors.name: search discoverability
factors.def: whether a documented technique can be found by someone who does not already know its name
factors.observable: search results for a described symptom

factors.name: copyright and reuse constraint
factors.def: whether the corpus may be redistributed, which decides what a public repo can hold
factors.observable: a source whose licence forbids republication

factors.name: citation stability
factors.def: whether an entry can cite something that will still exist
factors.observable: a citation to an archived snapshot

factors.name: the unread majority
factors.def: the fraction of the corpus no human has read, which is the honest limit of any claim of coverage
factors.observable: read rows against total rows

factors.name: what the record excludes by construction
factors.def: the classes of issue that never appear publicly, which bounds every corpus based claim
factors.observable: a mechanism with no public example despite being likely
